newsitem.title: JORDAN: U.S. grants $200 million loan to Jordan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. grants $200 million loan to Jordan.

text.p: Jordan signed an loan agreement on Saturday with Washington that provides $200 million worth of financing of U.S. imports to help boost bilateral trade, the state-run news agency Petra reported.

Jordan's Minister of Finance Marwan Awad signed the accord with U.S. Undersecretary of State for Economic and Business Affairs Joan Spero, currently visiting Amman for talks on boosting bilaterl economic ties.
"We know the challenges that face Jordan...and the loan will provide a spur to trade between the U.S. and Jordan," Spero was quoted as saying.
Petra gave no details of the loan's terms provided by the U.S. government's export promotion arm, the U.S. Export and Imports Bank.
The accord is part of about $1 billion of loans and grants pledged to Jordan by donor nations in a Paris consultative meeting last July that expressed support of the kingdom's economic reforms.

Spero, chairing her country's delegation in a new round of talks of the U.S.-Jordanian commission on economic cooperation, also discussed with senior Jordanian officials launching talks soon on a bilateral investment promotion accord and an open skies agreement.

Talks also focussed on progress in regional projects to underpin Middle East peace, including Jordan Rift Valley projects along the ridge seperating Jordan and Israel such as a multi-billion dollar scheme for a canal linking the Red Sea and Dead Sea.

They also discussed preparations for a Middle East economic summit in Cairo next November that Jordan, a key regional party, hopes will help attract foreign investors to multi-billion dollar projects it is promoting.
Egypt has expressed reservations about the summit saying would be pointless unless Israel made a serious effort to carry out peace talks with the Palestinians.
The conference is aimed at promoting economic integration between Israel and its neighbours.
